::: {#or-sensors}
| Sensor Category | Physical Principle & Spectral Range | Primary Target Variables for SMC Retrieval | Key Advantages & Limitations | References |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **RGB & Multispectral (MS)** <br> ![](../80_figures/81_icons/sensor_rgb.png){width=40} ![](../80_figures/81_icons/sensor_ms.png){width=40}| Passive optical sensors detecting reflected radiation in the visible (400–700 nm) and near-infrared (NIR, Red-Edge; 700–1000 nm) spectrum. | Vegetation indices (NDVI, NDRE, GNDVI), fraction of vegetation cover (FVC), structural and textural parameters (GLCM). | **Benefit:** High spatial resolution, low weight, affordability. <br>**Limits:** Inability to penetrate below the soil surface, signal is dependent on solar illumination and interfered with by cloud cover. | @Bhatti2020, @Chakhar2021, @Chandel2021, @Chaparro2024, @Chen2024, @Chu2026, @Feng2025, @Guo2026, @He2025, @Hussain2025, @Inocencio2025, @Liu2026, @Niu2022, @Niu2025, @PancheGil2025, @Rafi2026, @Shi2025, @Yin2024, @Young2025, @Zhang2023, @Zhang2026b |
| **Thermal Infrared (TIR)** <br> ![](../80_figures/81_icons/sensor_thermal.png){width=40}| Passive detection of emitted long-wave infrared radiation (LWIR; typically 8–14 µm) to estimate surface temperature. | Surface Temperature (LST), Crop Water Stress Index (CWSI), Temperature Vegetation Dryness Index (TVDI). | **Benefit:** Direct link to evapotranspiration and crop water stress. <br>**Limits:** Coarser spatial resolution compared to MS sensors, high dependence on microclimatic conditions (wind, air humidity). | @BasurtoLozada2020, @Bhatti2020, @Chandel2021, @Chu2026, @Liu2026, @Niu2022, @Shi2025, @Tauro2022, @Wang2024, @Yin2024, @Zhang2023 |
| **Hyperspectral (HS)** <br> ![](../80_figures/81_icons/sensor_hs.png){width=40}| Passive optical scanning in hundreds of narrow continuous bands (typically 400–1000 nm to 2500 nm). | Narrowband derivatives of reflectance, detailed physiological parameters of leaves (water content LWC, chlorophyll LCC). | **Benefit:** Extreme information density for deep physiological diagnostics. <br>**Limits:** Significant computational effort (*curse of dimensionality*), the need for complex data reduction (e.g. PLSR, PCA). | @Dopper2022, @Du2024, @Heistermann2023, @Liu2024, @Shokati2025 |
| **Microwave, GNSS-R & LiDAR** <br> ![](../80_figures/81_icons/sensor_microwave.png){width=40} ![](../80_figures/81_icons/sensor_lidar.png){width=40}| Passive reception of reflected GNSS signals (L-band) or active laser scanning (LiDAR) and georadar. | Estimate of surface reflectivity, 3D structure of the canopy, detection of subsurface anomalies. | **Benefit:** Ability to penetrate cloud cover and vegetation cover. <br>**Limits:** The signal is strongly distorted by surface roughness and complex biomass structure. | @Farhad2025, @Feng2025, @Rafi2026, @Senyurek2022, @Zajc2023 |
| **In-situ & IoT Sensors** <br>![](../80_figures/81_icons/probe.png){width=40} ![](../80_figures/81_icons/crns.png){width=40} | Contact measurement of dielectric permittivity (TDR, capacitance) in edge computing networks. | Absolute volumetric soil moisture (VWC) in the profile, calibration and reference (ground-truth) data. | **Benefit:** High accuracy and continuous recording in real time. <br>**Limits:** Strictly point coverage, invasiveness of measurement and limited areal scalability. | @Choudhari2024, @Keshavarz2025, @Soultane2024 |

Comprehensive classification of the sensor modalities applied in the reviewed studies, including their physical principles, target variables, and intrinsic limitations.
